question: Can bounded, recency-selected dormant memory correction capture some of the predictive benefit of a plurality-based global update with at most three corrective writes per detected event rather than all nine?
hypothesis: Updating the three newest dormant items may recover a nontrivial fraction of the immediate post-shift benefit of full plurality updates, with smaller compute and fewer unsupported changes.
domain: Same 16 cue identities, seven consecutive active cues episode(e)=(seed+3*episode+j)%16 for j0..6, 12 episodes, four target values and nine dormant slots from Y037. STABLE no change, MIXED_SWITCH from episode6 even cues +1 and odd cues +2 modulo4. Four overlapping live cues provide 2/2 contradictory deltas.
arms: baseline: regular observed-only dormant memory, no post-feedback correction
full_plurality: choose most frequent nonzero observed live-key delta with ties toward smaller value; apply to all dormant values
capped_three: identical plurality evidence and tie-break, but apply chosen delta only to the last three most recently inserted dormant entries according to the pre-existing OrderedDict LRU order
primary: Report heldout post-change correct, returning-dormant accuracy, per-seed comparison, total correction maintenance writes, unsupported evidence events, cache writes and occupancy. CAPPED_EFFICIENCY if capped post-change improvement over baseline is >= half of full plurality's improvement and total capped maintenance writes <=one third of full plurality's. HARM if capped worse than baseline; otherwise MIXED. Retain all outcomes and full budget cost.
safeguards: No true label formula available before each episode feedback; policy sees only observed current seven labels and previously cached data. No additional memory slots or target lookahead, exact frozen 7+9 cap and matched cache eviction/write trajectories, SHA256 distinct seeds, original artifact and full project regression, no post-result tuning or retry.
claim_limit: Synthetic recency-capped maintenance policy, not resource-efficient generalized cognition.
